title: Investigate stop-sequence default change causing truncated outputs and eval regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several large customers reported sudden quality regressions in nightly eval suites and production prompts after a serving runtime change that modified sampling defaults and the stop-sequence trimming behavior. The change surfaced as systematically shorter outputs, missing final tokens, or premature termination when customers relied on specific stop sequences. Affected deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private installs (after partner upgrades).

Observed symptoms:
- Automated eval scores dropped ~8-15% on multiple prompt suites for Acme Payments and NexHealth.
- Customer-reported production failures where downstream parsers failed due to truncated structured outputs.
- SDK-level streaming sometimes cut off at stop boundary when the final token was split across shards in batched inference.

Reproduction (high level):
1) Use the customer prompt set attached and model variant used by the customer (open-model-xq/quant-8).
2) Call /v1/generate with prior non-deterministic settings but with stop=["
END
"] and temperature default.
3) Observe that outputs sometimes end immediately before the literal stop sequence or with the last token dropped.

Initial hypothesis: A runtime change intended to make sampling deterministic for cached prefixes introduced a temperature floor and an optimization that aggressively trimmed trailing partial tokens when applying stop-sequence detection in the batched streaming path. When requests are batched or when KV cache boundaries align, the trim logic can drop the final byte(s) of a token, which in turn removes the literal stop sequence match and produces a truncated output.

Why this matters: Customers rely on exact stop sequences for structured outputs and evaluation harnesses. This regression caused false negatives in e2e tests and in-product failures for automated data processing.

Immediate impact: High for customers with strict parse-based integrations (billing, clinical workflows). Several customers opened escalations and paused deployments until the fix was available.

Desired outcome: Patch the runtime to restore previous stop-sequence semantics for existing customers, harden tests to catch similar regressions, and add a canary guard in rollout processes that checks sampled evals for token-level matches before shipping sampling/stop logic changes.
comments: 2026-03-10 Miguel Santos: Triage complete — reproduced in staging with customers' prompt sets. Root cause likely in streaming stop-match codepaths + sampling default change. Assigned to runtime team for hotfix.

2026-03-10 Claire Wong (PM): Notified Acme Payments and NexHealth. Offered immediate workaround: set stop_sequence_strict_override=true per-customer until patch. Customers accepted advisory and want ETA.

2026-03-11 Miguel Santos: Created PR (see attachments). Patch adds a compatibility flag that preserves legacy stop detection for batched/streaming inference; also disables temperature-flooring behavior when prefix_cache=true. Running integration tests against customer evals now.
2026-03-11 Infra (Jamal R.): Rolled rollback on hosted canary pool to v1.19.1 for affected shard; monitoring shows recovered eval metrics within 1 hour.
2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: Drafted customer communication with rollback details and private/Dedicated upgrade instructions. Scheduling postmortem 2026-03-16 10:00 UTC.

2026-03-12 Miguel Santos: Hotfix staged for Dedicated pools; provided upgrade artifact and private upgrade note to SEs. Still verifying that KV-cache edge-case is fully resolved across sequence lengths.
2026-03-12 Claire Wong: Escalation marked P0; Sales & Support looped in for compensation/credits if required.
investigation_notes: Checked diffs between runtime-1.19.0 and 1.19.1: sampling default change introduced temperature_floor=0.0 -> 0.01 in sampler.cc and added early_trim logic in stream_decoder.cc.
Reproduced truncation locally when batch_size>=3 and when the stop token crosses a KV cache boundary (observed with sequence lengths ~128-240).
Heap and trace logs show 'early_trim=true' in streaming path causing last token->byte truncation before stop-match routine.
Workaround validated: toggling stop_sequence_strict_override=true returns outputs to expected length and passes customer's nightly eval suite.
resolution: Rolled back the sampling/stop trimming change on hosted canaries and staged a compatibility-mode hotfix (runtime-1.19.2) that restores legacy stop-matching semantics for batched/streaming inference. Pushed hotfix artifact to Dedicated teams and distributed upgrade instructions for Private customers. Notified affected customers and provided temporary per-customer config override.
next_steps: Ship runtime-1.19.2 to hosted within 24 hours and monitor eval metrics for 48 hours post-deploy.
Add unit+integration tests that simulate token-boundary stop sequences across batching and KV cache boundaries (assigned ENG-9433).
Add a canary gate to rollout process: run a sampled customer eval suite and compare token-level stop-match success before enabling sampling/stop changes (process update in runtime release checklist).
Postmortem writeup and action owners (postmortem scheduled 2026-03-16).
Follow-up with customer success to confirm long-term acceptance and close escalations.
